Basic.ui_label: Enrich events using Account Number and Charge Name or Subscription Id

ZSO.ui_label: Enrich events using Product or Account data

AccountAndChargeName.description: Standard subscription lookup — resolves subscription and charge by account number and charge name. Fixed output fields: accountNumber, subscriptionNumber, chargeNumber, uom.

SubscriptionId.description: Lookup by subscription ID. Fixed output fields: accountNumber, subscriptionNumber, chargeNumber, uom.

Account.description: Prefetch-based enrichment from Account, Subscription, RatePlan, RatePlanCharge, ProductRatePlanCharge, or RatePlanChargeTier. mapFields is the join key (event field → reference field). appendFields defines which reference fields to append to the event.
Account.reference_field_syntax: Object.FieldName — e.g. Account.AccountNumber, Subscription.Name, RatePlanCharge.UOM, RatePlanChargeTier.StartingUnit

Product.description: Prefetch-based enrichment from Product, ProductRatePlan, ProductRatePlanCharge, or ProductRatePlanChargeTier. mapFields is the join key. appendFields defines output.

Advanced.description: Data Query enrichment using a custom SQL JOIN query. The sql field is a broad dataset query with no per-event binding. The backend executes it as: SELECT * FROM (<sql>) temp WHERE <mapFields join condition>. mapFields defines the event-to-SQL join key. appendFields defines which SQL columns to append to the event.
sql_notes: Write a broad JOIN query — do NOT put per-event WHERE conditions in the sql field
The backend wraps it at runtime: SELECT * FROM (<your sql>) temp WHERE <mapFields join condition> = <event value>
mapFields defines the join key: eventField is the event field name, referenceField is the SQL SELECT column alias
appendFields defines output: referenceField must match the SQL SELECT column alias exactly (bare alias, not table.column)
appendFields[].type is optional — set to 'number' for numeric columns, omit or set null for string (drives output schema type)
Supports JOINs across any Zuora Billing objects queryable via Data Query

example.sql: SELECT a.AccountNumber, s.Name AS SubscriptionNumber, rpc.ChargeNumber, rpc.UOM FROM Account a JOIN Subscription s ON s.AccountId = a.Id JOIN RatePlan rp ON rp.SubscriptionId = s.Id JOIN RatePlanCharge rpc ON rpc.RatePlanId = rp.Id

CustomObject.description: Prefetch-based enrichment using a tenant Custom Object. Requires prefetch v4 to be enabled on the tenant. referenceField uses namespace__objectname.fieldname__c syntax.

assumptions.reason: AccountAndChargeName is the most common enrichment type — matches by account number and charge name.
Drop events with no match. Set to true only if unmatched events should pass through with null enrichment fields.
Only match active or cancelled subscriptions; exclude draft/suspended/expired.
Include all rate plan charge segments by default. Set to true and provide eventTimeField only when segment date filtering is required.
Include all charge types unless the meter only processes usage charges.

blockers.message: Which event field contains the account number? (required for AccountAndChargeName lookup)
Which event field contains the charge name? (required for AccountAndChargeName lookup)
Which event field contains the subscription ID? (required for SubscriptionId lookup)
includeSegmentsActiveOnDateOnly is true — which event field contains the datetime for segment filtering?

mapFields is required for Account/Product/Advanced/CustomObject lookup. It is the join key the backend uses to match each event to a row in the enrichment dataset. Each entry: {eventField: <event field name>, referenceField: <SQL column alias or Object.FieldName>}.

appendFields is required. Each entry: {eventField: <name to write onto the event>, referenceField: <SQL column alias or Object.FieldName>}. For Advanced: referenceField must match the SQL SELECT alias exactly (bare alias, not table.column).

sql is required for Advanced lookup. Write a broad JOIN query with no per-event WHERE conditions — the backend adds the per-event filter automatically using mapFields. Example: SELECT a.AccountNumber, s.Name AS SubscriptionNumber FROM Account a JOIN Subscription s ON s.AccountId = a.Id
